<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Ports the spike POC (spike/004-cache-proxy 6566e91f) into the workspace as a product: crate, CLI verb with status/account/off/on, a config file, a LaunchAgent recipe pair, and receipts on plain `copilot` processes for matrix rows 2, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 22. The daemon side (spawn gate, receipts, notices, doctor row) is s03 and builds against the status route in parallel. One coder (pij-charming-crane).

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A plain `copilot` process pointed at the sidecar on a Claude model reads its context from a 1-hour cache after more than 5 minutes idle.
- The sidecar is the single holder of the account token and the single source of readiness truth the daemon reads, through a status route that matches blueprint 003 exactly.
- The sidecar never costs a launch per request and never loops on a failing refresh.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- The daemon side (s03): spawn gate, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` env at spawn, receipt, seat proxy state, 30 s watch and prime notices, directory and doctor rows. s03 calls this plan's dscl parser from doctor.
- Installing either LaunchAgent on this machine; bouncing or deploying the prod daemon.
- A generic `pij config` store (blueprint d-5).
- Proactive token refresh (blueprint d-3: the `gho_` token has no expiry).
- A business-account receipt for row 14 if no business account is available on this machine; the gap is named, not faked.

## Acceptance criteria

| id | claim | state | note | receipt | pressure | proven_by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ac-0001 | Rewrite and pass-through (req-01, req-07, req-13). On `POST /v1/messages*` with a JSON body: every `cache_control` of type `ephemeral` without a `ttl` gets `ttl: "1h"` (an explicit ttl is kept); `X-Initiator` is `agent` when the last message is a user message made only of `tool_result` blocks, else `user`; a `*-1m` model is forwarded as its base id and logged `model=&lt;base&gt; (from &lt;x&gt;-1m)`. Only `anthropic-version`, `anthropic-beta`, `content-type` and `accept` pass from the client, plus the Copilot identity headers and the held bearer. Status, `content-type`, `request-id`, `x-request-id` and `retry-after` come back, and the body streams through unchanged (SSE, tool use, images, 1M context). Non-JSON or other paths pass through byte-for-byte. Receipts: rows 2, 15, 16, 22. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0002 | Token holder (req-02, req-03, req-10). `gh` is resolved once at start to an absolute path (`PIJ_GH` if set and absolute and executable, else PATH) and launched as `gh auth token --user &lt;account&gt;` only at start, on an account change, on a reload when the account changed, no token is held or the last fetch or refresh failed, and on a 401. Each launch is counted as `gh.cache_proxy_token`. The token lives in memory only: never logged, written or put in argv. A 401 triggers one single-flight refresh shared by every waiting request (a request that saw an older token generation reuses the newer one without launching) and one retry per request with the refreshed token; a 401 with no newer token (refresh failed or latched) is returned to the seat, not retried. A refresh's result, success or failure, lands only if the holder is still the account and generation it was fetched for, so a refresh for account A never replaces account B's token after a switch (#239 F001). A failed refresh keeps the current token, sets state `no_token` once, and latches: no further refresh until a reload, so a burst of 401s after a failed refresh launches nothing. Test-only `PIJ_CACHE_PROXY_TEST_STALE_TOKEN=1` swaps the token for a stale one after the readiness check. Receipts: rows 9, 10, 11, 17. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0003](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0003 | Readiness (req-06, req-13). With the token: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/user` gives `endpoints.api` (the upstream) and `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` (usable if `unlimited`, `remaining &gt; 0` or `overage_permitted`; else `quota.reset` from `quota_reset_date`); `GET &lt;endpoints.api&gt;/models` gives `models`: every id starting `claude` and not ending `-1m`, keyed by id, with `capabilities.limits.max_prompt_tokens`. Both are cached per account for 10 minutes and re-run lazily on the next status read after expiry, after a successful refresh, and after a 402. A 402 from upstream latches `quota_exhausted` at once; a lagging snapshot that still says usable never clears it, only a 2xx from `/v1/messages`, the snapshot's `quota_reset_date` passing, or a reload (pm-004 ruling on #239 F002). Facts read with a token since replaced by a reload or refresh are dropped. No timer, no poll inside the sidecar. Receipt: row 14 (enterprise and personal hosts in the log), row 5 refusal for jakkaj. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0005](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0004 | Status route matches blueprint 003 c-status-route exactly. `GET /__pij/status` returns `{ready, state, reason, fix, account, upstream_host, quota: {usable, reset}, models: {&lt;base id&gt;: {max_prompt_tokens}}, counters: {requests, refreshes, gh_launches, upstream_401, upstream_402}, pid, since}` and nothing else. `ready` is true only in state `ready`. `state` is one of `ready`, `off`, `no_account`, `gh_missing`, `no_token`, `quota_exhausted`, `upstream_unreachable`. Types: `reason`/`fix` strings (empty when ready), `account`/`upstream_host`/`quota.reset` string or null, `quota.usable` bool, counters and `pid` integers, `since` epoch milliseconds when `state` last changed. `POST /__pij/reload` takes no body, re-reads the config, refetches the token if the account changed or none is held or the last refresh failed, re-runs readiness, and returns the status object. No token, header value or secret appears in either. A golden test pins the key set and state names. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0007](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0005 | Loopback only, browser-safe. The listener binds 127.0.0.1 only (port 7471; `--port` or `PIJ_CACHE_PROXY_PORT` for tests). Any request with an `Origin` header, or a `Host` that is not `127.0.0.1:&lt;port&gt;` or `localhost:&lt;port&gt;`, gets 403 before anything is forwarded, so a web page or DNS rebinding can't spend the account. Requests that arrive while no token is held get 503 with an Anthropic-shaped error naming the state and fix. Request bodies are capped at 64 MiB. The upstream client follows no redirect, so a 3xx can't carry the bearer token to another host (#239 security note). | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0008](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0006 | Verb and config (req-02). `pij-rs cache-proxy` runs the sidecar in the foreground (an early branch beside `daemon`, before any daemon client). `pij-rs cache-proxy status` prints state, reason, fix, account, upstream host, quota, models and counters (`--json`: the envelope, `data.{port, listening, status, fix, config_written, accounts_warning, accounts_error}`, `status` being the status object), or `not listening on 127.0.0.1:&lt;port&gt;` plus the fix, and then the second-human-account warning when it applies. `account &lt;login&gt;`, `off` and `on` write `&lt;state-dir&gt;/cache-proxy.toml` (`account`, `enabled`; default state dir `~/.pij-rs`, same precedence as every pij-rs verb) atomically with mode 0600, then POST reload; if nothing listens they say the change applies at next start. No file or no account is `no_account`; `enabled = false` is `off`. `off` stops new spawns being proxied (ready false) but keeps serving live seats with the held token. Changing the account takes effect for the next request. | [x] checked | — | — | [bp-0009](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0007 | Second-human-account check (row 19, req-11 groundwork). A pure parser of `/usr/bin/dscl . -list /Users UniqueID` output returns the human accounts (uid 501 and up, excluding `nobody`-style and `_`-prefixed system names); a unit test with two human accounts yields the warning and with one yields none. `status` launches dscl once per run (recorded as `dscl.cache_proxy_accounts`); never on a timer. <a id="testing-strategy"></a>

## Testing Strategy

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| approach | Unit tests on pure functions (rewrite, readiness parse, status shape, config, dscl parser); one integration test file driving the real router against a fake upstream and a fake gh script; live rows on plain copilot processes for what only the real endpoint can show. |
| rationale | Single-flight, the failed-refresh latch, 402 handling and Origin refusal are concurrency and boundary behaviour a reviewer can't see from code; the fake upstream makes them deterministic. Cache, billing and model names need the real API. |
| focus_areas | single-flight refresh count; latch; exact status key set; Origin/Host refusal; -1m mapping; quota rule |
| excluded | daemon spawn gate and notices (s03); launchctl installation |
| mock_usage | Fake upstream and fake gh only at the process/HTTP edge; no mocks inside the crate. |

| s03 builds against the status route in parallel and reads type details the blueprint leaves open (since, quota.reset, reason when ready). | Medium | High | AC4 fixes the types; send them to pm-004 with the plan; a golden test pins the key set. No contract change without pm-004. |
| Row 11 by `gh auth logout` would log the shared account out of every seat's gh. | High | High | Simulate with a PIJ_GH wrapper that succeeds once and then fails; the fake-upstream test covers 'keeps serving with the current token'. |

| Live rows spend premium requests and need a 6+ minute idle wait. | High | Low | jorkni_microsoft (overage permitted); jakkaj only for the quota refusal; short prompts. |
| Shared cargo target with coder 229; disk floor. | Medium | Medium | shared-build only, -p scoping, one build per change; stop and tell pm-004 on a disk-floor refusal. |
| `off` while seats are proxied: cutting them would break live turns. | Medium | Medium | `off` only clears ready (new spawns plain); the held token keeps serving live seats. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Builds only via `PIJ_SHARED_TARGET=<pi-hacking>/target-ws004 just shared-build`, -p scoped, one at a time; disk-floor refusal → stop and tell pm-004.
- Never restart, bounce or deploy the prod daemon; never install either LaunchAgent; plist proven with plutil -lint on a temp path.
- Never read credential files or print a token; tokens only flow through pipes (`gh auth token` stdout, `curl -H @-`).
- Test clients are plain copilot processes in tmux session ws004-s02-test on its own socket; test port, not 7471; never type into a pane I didn't create.
- Status route contract is shared with s03: no change without pm-004.
- Stage by path; no `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, no refs/notes push; trailers Pij-Seat, Pij-Prime pij-far-jackal, Pij-Plan 228-cache-proxy-sidecar.
